author: Fr. José Mª de J. González (Gobernador Eclesiástico de Ambas Californias)
summary: THE FALSE-BISHOP WARNING: 'Más ha de un mes que arribó al Puerto de San Francisco un sujeto que dice llamarse Juan Bautista Brignole, asegurando ser Obispo Legado Apostólico *urbis et orbis*, y Superior General Reformador de la Religión Católica, Secular, Regular, y Monástica en la República Mexicana y sus adyacentes; y de hecho ha comenzado ya á ejercer su jurisdicción deforme por escrito, contraviniendo á dos Religiosos, los Padres Branchi y Romani, que probablemente han llegado también á este país; dicho Señor Obispo y Legado Pontificio se ha presentado sin comitiva, y con una vestimenta tan extraña á su elevado carácter, que la primera vez que visitó al Padre Ministro de San Francisco fue envuelto en un zarape azul, diciendo le habían robado su equipaje...' — González warns the govt that a personage of such high category never travels absolutely alone; asks the civil authorities' help to recover his effects or, failing that, that they not redound in disrepute; ⭐⭐⭐ a self-proclaimed itinerant 'Bishop & Apostolic Legate' (Brignole) unmasked as a probable impostor wandering conquest-era California in a blue serape
cite: Miscellaneous / Unbound Documents, MS, Archives of California, BANC MSS C-A 63, Bancroft Library, University of California, Berkeley; Savage transcript p. 364 (original destroyed 1906; digitized scan n366–367)

summary: THE STA BÁRBARA BOUNDARY & REPRESENTATION PROTEST: encloses an acta in which the Pueblo of Sta Bárbara resolved to make observations on the 3-Jun-1849 Riley proclamation (the civil-govt plan of the country); a first observation objects to the new marking of California district limits, by which part of Sta Bárbara's inhabitants & extension of its population would pass to Los Ángeles & San Luis Obispo, to the detriment of their interests — the Pueblo asks the limits of Sta Bárbara on the south side remain as the Assembly marked them in 1846; a second observation: Sta Bárbara has not been given the representation due it at the Convention, while other districts of lesser population were assigned 4 or 5 delegates & Sta Bárbara only 2; objects to the appointment of supernumerary/suplente delegates; signed Pablo de la Guerra (Presidente), Antonio María de la Guerra & Raymundo Carrillo (Secretarios) — ⭐⭐ a Californio protest against under-representation at the 1849 constitutional convention

summary: THE BAJA-CALIFORNIA ARMISTICE: avisa que el 27 de Febrero se firmó un armisticio por el Gobierno Mexicano, y el Ministro Americano (cuya copia le remite) le ordena que, cumpliendo con lo mandado en el Art. 1º, disponga que tanto en los puntos ocupados por el ejército americano (desde el 5 de Marzo) como en los que no lo estén, se proceda á elegir las autoridades que deben gobernar al Territorio como parte de la Confederación Mexicana; dice que no debe extrañarse que él lo escriba desde Mazatlán, lugar ocupado por el enemigo, porque le ha sido preciso tener unas conferencias con el Comandante de las Fuerzas Navales á instancia suya sobre dicho armisticio — ⭐⭐ the 27-Feb-1848 armistice / end of the U.S.-Mexican war reaching the Californias via Mazatlán

summary: THE CASTRO SELF-VINDICATION: supposes that by this date Mason has received his communication dated at San Luis Obispo relative to his arrival at that point; today received Mason's letter of the 7th manifesting the informes given re a revolution in which Castro is said to be implicated; it may well be that the delay of his march gave his enemies occasion to detract from his reputation in that manner; assures Mason it is all an atrocious imposture, that tomorrow he will have the satisfaction of clearing himself in His Excellency's presence & testify to the authorities now governing the Dept of his sane intention in returning, & his gratitude for the kindnesses shown; assures he will always contribute all in his power to maintain the peace & tranquility of 'este país en que ví la luz primera y que amo como el primero de sus hijos'; 'los impostores no serán jamás capaces de mirar con sentimientos con el que tiene el honor de repetirse su sincero amigo y servidor' — ⭐⭐ José Castro's formal denial of being a conquest-era revolutionary conspirator

author: Henry S. Burton (Col. of N.Y. Volunteers) — Información Sumaria
summary: THE PADRE GABRIEL GONZÁLEZ WAR-CONDUCT INQUIRY: Col. Burton ordered (13 Apr 1848) an examination of witnesses Guadalupe González, Andrés Hipólito, y [Félix] Morales (vecinos of Todos Santos, residents at La Paz) on the participation of Padre Gabriel González in the war of Baja California [against the U.S.]; witness González declared the Mexican force came to those parts & he heard that from Gonzaga [González] había recibido una carta de Manuel Pineda (Comte Principal de Baja Calª) communicating the prompt arrival of Anaya; witness Andrés Hipólito (alcalde of Todos Santos, Nov 1847) said that when the American troops arrived, the Padre sent a courier to the nearest Mexican force chief warning him; the Padre imagined the Mexican force was coming to attack the Americans & that the Padre González — fearing the roll[?] of the Mexican flag — had his horses stolen; witness Morales declared that when the Mexican force approached, the Padre had ordered the Mayordomo of that [mission] to take up arms against the American force, saying 'que no era razón que unos estuvieran durmiendo con sus mujeres, mientras otros estaban peleando por la Patria' — ⭐⭐⭐ a war-crimes/loyalty inquiry into a missionary priest's active support of Mexican resistance during the U.S. conquest of Baja California
cite: Miscellaneous / Unbound Documents, MS, Archives of California, BANC MSS C-A 63, Bancroft Library, University of California, Berkeley; Savage transcript p. 381 (original destroyed 1906; digitized scan n381–383)

author: Fr. Gabriel González ↔ Manuel Pineda (Comte Principal de Baja Cal.)
place: Rancho San Jacinto / Todos Santos (Baja Cal.)
summary: THE PINEDA–GONZÁLEZ BAJA-WAR CORRESPONDENCE (continuous dossier attached to the Burton inquiry, doc 513): a run of letters between Padre Gabriel González & the Mexican commander Manuel Pineda during the anti-American campaign in Baja California — (Nov 10) González advises that to arrange the operations in the campaign against the Americans it is well to rely on the Junta Territorial, so the pueblo not blame the Padre directly for the war contributions imposed; (Nov 21) congratulates Pineda on the energy shown against the foreign enemy, recommends he provide himself with pólvora as an indispensable element, & notes that at La Magdalena there are French & Dutch vessels whose captains disapprove of the U.S. war, advising Pineda give a safe-conduct to individuals he can send to buy powder from those vessels; (Nov 24) learns (by Pineda's letter) he is accused before the Comandancia Principal of conspiring against the Mexican arms & the country's independence, protests his conduct is irreproachable 'como lo ha probado manifestando en público y á la faz del enemigo sus ideas patrióticas'; (Feb 1, 1848) a long self-defense — 'la sangre derramada el año de [18]42 por más que se quiso culparme como Ud lo hace ahora'; the public is undeceived in the sinister designs; asks that, to prove his good intentions, he be given a pasaporte ó salvo conducto para Loreto ó Mulegé so he may embark for Sonora or some other point in the Republic — ⭐⭐⭐ documentary core of a missionary's role in the Mexican resistance to the U.S. conquest of Baja California, and his self-exculpation

author: Los residentes
summary: THE MINERS' PETITION vs THE ABOLITION OF THE MINING ORDINANCES: the undersigned residents & natives of the Department represent that they have seen with sorrow the superior decree of 12 Feb suspending the abolition[sic] of the mining ordinances of the Mexican Republic — an important branch of universal mining observed in the Mexican Republic; that by the various proclamations of the U.S. commanders it was manifested that Mexican laws not militating against military possession of this country (acquired by right of war) would be observed until a definitive peace treaty ceded the department; the 12 Feb order to destroy this hope has annihilated the brilliant prospect of the mining spirit; mining cannot be developed without the safeguard of the wise laws that the 'única potencia del mundo' [Mexico] gave, knowing the little aptitude of the laborers & cattle-raisers to discover & work minerals; on the 'lesión enorme' the rancheros suffer for metallic discoveries in their lands, it is a manifest error, for the ordenanza does not indemnify the costly piece of terreno occupied but results in a great increase of value to their properties by proximity of mining operations, which bring a great concurrence of operarios & cause diseminación de dinero; the said decree has caused notable prejudice to many persons who erected costly works in soliciting veins; supplicate the execution of the decree be suspended until the U.S. govt resolves on the matter — ⭐⭐ a substantial gold-rush-era petition defending Mexican mining law against American suspension (companion to the Cambuston quicksilver case, doc 439)
